You are a blind semantic decoder of natural-language crystal descriptions. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Read its spatial meaning, identify the coordinate convention and symmetry, resolve numerical relations, and produce a finite crystal construction plan. Do not assume unstated positional values, look up a named material, or claim a complete reconstruction when required information is missing.
Return one JSON object only, without a Markdown fence. For a complete conventional-cell description use this schema:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"literal Hall symbol specified in the prose","lattice":[a,b,c,alpha,beta,gamma],"composition":{"Element":integer_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[fractional_x,fractional_y,fractional_z]}]}
Lengths are in angstroms and angles in degrees. Copy the Hall symbol from the description, preserving its mathematical meaning; the geometry engine resolves the public-table integer index, so do not guess a Hall number. Each representative may be any equivalent point of that Wyckoff orbit in the declared Hall setting. List each independent orbit once; multiple orbits of the same element remain separate. The geometry engine will apply all public Hall-setting symmetry operations, retain unique points per orbit, and write the full unit cell. Sites have full occupancy in this pilot.
Use the supplied meanings and numbers rather than matching any fixed wording. You may rely on public crystallographic definitions to identify a Wyckoff orbit or Hall convention. If the text does not determine the necessary lattice, independent positions or setting, return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for incompatible constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Do not output guessed coordinates to fill missing information.

The crystal is orthorhombic, belonging to the body-centered space group Imma (No. 74, Hall symbol −I 2b 2), with lattice parameters a = 6.03 Å, b = 6.13 Å, and c = 8.45 Å and all three interaxial angles fixed at 90°. Fractional coordinates are given along a, b, and c in the standard Hall frame, which coincides with the original input frame. The unit cell contains eight lithium, four vanadium, four nickel, and sixteen oxygen atoms, all sites being fully occupied.

The cations occupy four distinct fourfold orbits, each sitting on a special position with no free coordinate parameters. Nickel atoms occupy the 4a site at (0, 0, 0), placing them at the corners and, through the body-centering translation, at the cell center. Vanadium atoms occupy the 4c site at (1/4, 1/4, 1/4), so each vanadium is displaced by one quarter of each cell edge from a nickel position. The eight lithium atoms divide equally between two inequivalent fourfold sites: half reside on the 4b position at (0, 0, 1/2), lying directly above and below the nickel atoms at half the c-axis height, while the other half occupy the 4d position at (1/4, 1/4, 3/4), displaced a quarter along a and b and three quarters along c. Together with the Imma centering, these four orbits generate a regular three-dimensional cation framework in which Ni, V, and the two Li sublattices alternate at quarter-interval heights along c.

The sixteen oxygen atoms are distributed over two independent eightfold orbits, each carrying two free positional parameters. The first oxygen orbit, on the 8i site, has coordinates (x, 1/4, z) with x = 0.237 and z = 0.995; these atoms are therefore confined to mirror planes at b = 1/4 (and its symmetry equivalents), lying very close to the top and bottom faces of the cell along c while shifted roughly a quarter of the way along a. The second oxygen orbit, on the 8h site, has coordinates (0, y, z) with y = 0.027 and z = 0.76; these atoms lie in the a = 0 face planes, positioned just off the b = 0 edge at a fractional height of 0.76 along c. All oxygen positions are fully occupied, and the combination of the 8i and 8h orbits with the body-centering operation completes the anion sublattice surrounding the Ni, V, and Li cation arrays.
